scope: GPT-SoVITS inference residency, reference preprocessing, acceleration and quantization candidates that may preserve an existing v2 fine-tuned voice.

baseline.existing_tts: GPT-SoVITS v2 custom fine-tuned GPT/SoVITS checkpoints
baseline.compatibility_requirement: Keep the existing voice checkpoints, reference audio/text and Chinese conditioning; a different base model or disabled BERT is not an equivalent voice-preserving optimization.
reference_baseline_observations: TTS already has prompt_cache and set_ref_audio: reference semantic tokens and spectrogram are reused.
Unchanged reference text also reuses phones and BERT features; warm reference caching is not a newly discovered capability absent from v2.
The model initializer still loads GPT, SoVITS, BERT and CNHuBERT. Cache reuse alone does not establish lower resident model memory.
The release tag is a comparison reference, not a claim that deployed local patches are identical to the tag.

candidates.ownership: Official inference implementation; explicit residency changes would be a local adaptation.
candidates.version: 20240821v2 reference behavior, also present in reviewed official main b4570b876f5c086819ba84e3215472733c6a7b70
capabilities: Reuse reference semantic tokens, reference spectrogram, reference phones and reference BERT features.
A fixed-voice deployment can investigate retaining derived tensors while actually releasing an unneeded reference encoder.
candidates.v2_checkpoint_compatibility: Preserves existing checkpoint architecture; no voice retraining is inherently required for feature reuse.
limitations: Explicit encoder release and reload-on-reference-change are not established by ordinary prompt_cache reuse.
Arbitrary new Chinese output text still needs its own frontend/BERT features; caching the reference cannot precompute unknown future text.
Cache invalidation must include model/checkpoint, reference contents, reference language/text, preprocessing and precision.
Cold reference extraction may still dominate peak memory even if warm residency decreases.
candidates.torch27_cuda128_fit: Most direct route within the existing Torch runtime; no new execution-provider stack is required for reuse alone.

capabilities: Native Torch SDPA with CUDA Graph; optional external FlashAttention; ordinary inference fallback when an acceleration capability is unavailable.
Serial bs=1 and parallel inference are distinct paths.
candidates.v2_checkpoint_compatibility: The maintenance note reports v2 TTS execution; the adapter loads existing GPT weights. This is not an automatic upgrade of a v2 voice to a new SoVITS generation.

author_validation.reported_tests: Graph/parallel combinations and fallback cases produced audio.

limitations: CUDA Graph and static KV buffers may trade memory for latency; speed improvement does not establish lower peak RAM.
The integrated accelerator can coexist with the original TTS model object; inspect duplicate resident AR weights before claiming savings.
Windows FlashAttention wheels and bundled DLL handling do not transfer to Linux aarch64.
Keep a genuine bs=1 capacity and validate real checkpoint behavior instead of copying a large parallel batch default.
candidates.torch27_cuda128_fit: Pure Torch SDPA/Graph is the closest acceleration candidate to the existing runtime; extra FlashAttention is optional and not assumed available.

candidates.quantized_scope: AR Transformer self.h only; this is not all GPT-SoVITS components, activations or a complete INT8 TTS distribution.
candidates.v2_checkpoint_compatibility: Conversion starts from loaded GPT checkpoint weights, so the voice checkpoint need not be replaced; pronunciation, prosody and output validity still need comparison.
limitations: Ordinary AccelInference and create_acceleration do not expose/pass quantize_mode in the reviewed integration; this is not an existing API toggle.
BERT, CNHuBERT, SoVITS, KV/Graph buffers and runtime workspaces are outside the demonstrated INT8 scope.
No measured MiB saving is claimed: the actually quantized parameter set, scales, duplicate weights and runtime peak have not been measured.
Current TorchAO releases have raised minimum PyTorch requirements; do not install an unpinned latest TorchAO into Torch 2.7.
A legacy TorchAO version with the required Int8WeightOnlyConfig interface exists, but exact Torch 2.7/CUDA12.8/aarch64 binary or source-build compatibility remains unverified.
FP8 alternatives have additional hardware gates and are not established as a Jetson fallback.

capabilities: Detects v1/v2 SoVITS embeddings and exports GPT encoder/decoder stages and VITS ONNX graphs.
candidates.v2_checkpoint_compatibility: Exporter consumes custom GPT/SoVITS checkpoint paths; a v2 conversion route exists without changing to a different TTS family.
limitations: Export code is not proof of a maintained end-to-end INT8 or TensorRT release.
No Jetson quality, dynamic-shape, latency or peak-RAM result was collected.
Aarch64 ONNX Runtime GPU/TensorRT execution-provider availability must be checked against the actual CUDA/cuDNN/JetPack environment.
ONNX file size is distinct from session weights, buffers, execution-provider workspaces and cold conversion/build peaks.

candidates.ownership: Independent implementation maintained by chinokikiss/mahir0; not represented here as an official RVC-Boss release.
capabilities: Loader directly reads existing .ckpt and .pth checkpoints.
cache_prompt_audio caches prompt features and normally sets CNHuBERT to None afterward.
cache_spk_audio normally releases the SV model after caching.
Native Torch CUDA path, optional FlashAttention, CUDA Graph and cached runtime buffers.
candidates.v2_checkpoint_compatibility: A concrete loader path exists for original v2 checkpoints; that does not establish audio equivalence with this project’s custom voice.

author_measurements.measurement_boundary: Author-reported GPU VRAM, not verified whole-machine peak RSS/RAM; cold reference extraction, exact BERT setting and measurement method are not fully specified in the comparison table.

limitations: Constructor defaults use_bert=False. An equivalent Chinese comparison must explicitly retain BERT rather than silently changing conditioning.
Default checkpoint paths are newer base models; explicitly load the existing v2 voice instead.
SDK defaults disentangle speaker/style conditioning; preserve the same reference inputs when evaluating voice compatibility.
Its CPU BERT branch uses an INT8 ONNX frontend; this is not evidence of a fully INT8 CUDA TTS model.
No upstream aarch64/Jetson validation was found in the reviewed material.
Additional package/ONNX Runtime dependencies need an isolated compatibility check; do not replace the existing Torch installation.
candidates.torch27_cuda128_fit: Worth a controlled native-Torch trial with BERT enabled and FlashAttention optional; existing-runtime compatibility is a hypothesis, not a passed result.

candidates.ownership: Independent GPT-SoVITS-Devel implementation; not represented here as an official RVC-Boss release.
capabilities: ONNX and TensorRT FP16 routes, preallocated KV buffers and bounded shape profiles.
Export consumes original custom GPT/SoVITS checkpoint paths; examples target v2ProPlus and version detection includes v2.
candidates.v2_checkpoint_compatibility: A v2-family conversion path is present, but current custom-v2 voice behavior has not been validated locally; do not substitute its demonstration voice.

author_measurements.measurement_boundary: Author VRAM table does not establish Jetson shared-DRAM peak memory. In the table ONNX/TRT use more VRAM than original PyTorch despite speed improvements.

limitations: TensorRT engines must be built for the actual hardware/CUDA/TensorRT combination; do not reuse a desktop serialized engine.
Small/fitted profiles limit maximum per-segment shapes/audio; changing them must preserve intended utterance support rather than truncate output.
requirements.txt installs onnxruntime on aarch64/arm64 and onnxruntime-gpu only on x86_64/AMD64; stock installation does not establish GPU ONNX execution on Jetson.
Exporter requires additional frontend/SV assets and uses newer ONNX opsets; export success and runtime parser support need validation.
No current-v2 Jetson/Torch2.7/CUDA12.8 complete benchmark or ready full-chain INT8 release was established.

version_boundaries.v2: Existing fine-tuned voice baseline. Its reference frontend and synthesis architecture should remain explicit in comparisons.
version_boundaries.v2pro_and_v2proplus: Add SV conditioning and larger acoustic models; these are not intrinsically lighter than v2 and are not interchangeable v2 fine-tuned checkpoints.
version_boundaries.v3_and_v4: Use a different CFM-DiT acoustic path and additional vocoder requirements. Switching to them is not a drop-in compression of an existing v2 voice.
version_boundaries.other_tts_families: A smaller alternative TTS model cannot directly consume the current GPT-SoVITS v2 voice checkpoints; treat any switch as a voice/quality migration, not a transparent optimization.

measurement_rules: Keep checkpoint identity, reference audio/text, Chinese BERT conditioning and utterance set fixed when claiming a voice-preserving improvement.
Record artifact weight size separately from process resident memory, Torch allocated/reserved memory, runtime/engine workspaces and whole-machine available RAM.
On Jetson, CPU and iGPU share physical SoC DRAM. Moving a model from CUDA to CPU alone does not demonstrate a lower whole-machine memory footprint.
Measure cold model/reference load, first complete non-silent utterance, warm repeated utterances and LLM-plus-TTS co-residency separately.
CUDA Graph/static KV allocation, compilation and TensorRT build workspace can offset smaller weights; report peaks rather than only post-warm steady allocation.
Validate complete non-silent WAV, actual browser playback and voice/pronunciation quality; an HTTP 200, smaller file or faster first packet is insufficient.

recommended_order.reason: First check what is already cached; investigate actual CNHuBERT release after fixed-reference preprocessing while retaining the original voice and Chinese frontend.
Concrete direct checkpoint loader and auxiliary-model release make it worth comparing, with BERT explicitly enabled and original reference conditioning.
Native Torch candidate for latency, using bs=1; independently inspect duplicate residency and graph-buffer peak before treating it as a memory fix.
Evaluate only after confirming a compatible pinned TorchAO on the existing runtime; quantify its limited AR-only benefit and voice quality.
Defer conversion/engine integration until execution-provider compatibility and memory budgets are known; available author numbers do not show automatic memory reduction.

decision: Research candidates only. Keep user-selected MiniCPM5-2B and the existing v2 voice/runtime unchanged. No candidate has passed a Jetson validation in this review.
